title: Component
description:
Guiding question: Where does it live, and what is it responsible for?

A component is a cohesive part of the compiled product with one responsibility. Every file that lands in the compiled executable belongs to exactly one component. Components describe the current structure of the implementation: purpose, boundaries, prohibitions and permitted dependencies. They never describe tests, build scripts or release scripts.

id.description: Permanent, unique identifier. IDs must never be reused.

name.description: Short name of the responsibility, not of a file or module.

purpose.description: One sentence stating why this component exists.
examples: Runs deterministic checks and reports their outcomes.

scope.description: What the component is responsible for. Each entry is one responsibility stated as a complete sentence.

description.description: Something a reader might expect here that this component deliberately does not do.

owner.description: The component that is responsible instead. Omit it when no component owns the matter.

out_of_scope.description: Plausible responsibilities that belong elsewhere. They mark the boundary and point to the component that takes over.

must_not.description: Prohibitions for the code of this component that hold even when a task seems to call for them. A prohibition is not a boundary: out_of_scope says whose job something is, must_not says what is forbidden.

files.description: Every file of the component as a path relative to the repository root. No wildcards, no directories. A file may appear in exactly one component.

depends_on.description: Components whose code this component uses. The list must equal the dependencies found in the source files.
